Priya (docs): Hey all — small but blocking docs PR: our new example for function/tool calling shows the SDK returning a single final response with the function result merged into `choices[0].message.content`. Reviewer flagged that as inconsistent with runtime behavior. Preview CI #3456: https://ci.redwood/preview/3456

Alex (reviewer): Yep, in the docs example we do: "tool_output will appear in choices[0].message.content". That's what confused me because I hit the streaming path in the runtime and got delta events for the function call and a separate `tool_call` event.

Jorge (runtime): Correct — runtime emits function call events as streaming deltas (type: `tool_call` / `tool_output`) and does not automatically synthesize/merge the tool output into the final assistant message. Some higher-level SDK helpers may optionally merge for convenience, but the raw API surface intentionally separates the tool call stream from assistant content to make tool handling explicit.

Priya (docs): Thanks — can you give me the exact short wording we should use in the docs so the example is accurate? Also: is there an opt-in behavior we should document (e.g., SDK auto-merge) and which SDKs support it?

Ellen (sdk): Our Python SDK has a `auto_merge_tool_output=True` param on the high-level `chat()` helper (introduced last quarter). JS doesn't yet have that convenience flag; we currently expose the deltas via the event stream and leave merging to the app. So docs should not claim the API returns merged content by default.

Jorge (runtime): Suggested sentence: "Function/tool calls are delivered as distinct events (e.g., `tool_call` and `tool_output`) in streaming responses; the serving runtime does not merge tool results into the assistant message. SDKs may provide convenience helpers that perform merging — check the SDK-specific sections for availability and example code."

Priya (docs): Perfect. I'll replace the example and add two snippets: one raw-stream handling (showing event types) and one convenience snippet for Python `auto_merge_tool_output=True`. Ellen, can you paste a minimal Python example we can copy?

Ellen (sdk): sure — minimal example:
```python
# high-level helper that merges tool outputs (optional)
resp = client.chat(model="redwood/rw-chat-1", input=messages, auto_merge_tool_output=True)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
And raw stream handler (JS pseudocode):
```javascript
for await (const evt of client.streamChat(...)) {
  if (evt.type === 'tool_call') handleToolCall(evt);
  if (evt.type === 'tool_output') captureToolOutput(evt);
  if (evt.type === 'assistant_delta') appendAssistantDelta(evt);
}
// app merges outputs if desired
```

Alex (reviewer): That works. Also flagging to add a short migration note: customers who relied on old docs that implied auto-merge may need to update app logic when migrating to streaming-first handlers.

Jorge (runtime): Migration note: non-breaking. Only affects apps that assumed merged content from the transport layer. Recommend searching repos for `choices[0].message.content` usages after enabling streaming. We'll open a tiny runtime docs PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1302

Priya (docs): Great — I'll push the updated example and the two snippets. I'll add a callout pointing to the Python helper and a note that JS doesn't auto-merge yet with a follow-up SDK issue link. Updating now and re-running preview.
